title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Chronicles chapter 11 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Chronicles Chapter 11.

questions.question: In 2 Chronicles 11, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The word of the LORD comes to Shemaiah
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:1 describes Rehoboam gathering 180,000 warriors before the other events occur.

questions.question: How many chosen men did Rehoboam gather according to 2 Chronicles 11?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:1 states that Rehoboam gathered a hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men.

questions.question: Who received the word of the LORD in 2 Chronicles 11?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:2 says the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God.

questions.question: To whom did Shemaiah speak the word of the LORD?
options: Rehoboam and all Israel in Judah and Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam and all Israel in Judah and Benjamin
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:3 states Shemaiah was to speak to Rehoboam and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin.

questions.question: What did the LORD command Rehoboam and the people in 2 Chronicles 11?
options: Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren
Build a great army to conquer Israel
Send envoys to Jeroboam for peace
questions.correctAnswer: Ye shall not go up, nor fight against your brethren
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:4 quotes the LORD commanding them not to fight against their brethren.

questions.question: What was the reason given by the LORD for not fighting against Jeroboam?
options: For this thing is done of me
questions.correctAnswer: For this thing is done of me
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:4 explains the LORD said the matter was done by His will.

questions.question: Where did Rehoboam dwell after the command from the LORD?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:5 states that Rehoboam dwelt in Jerusalem.

questions.question: What type of cities did Rehoboam build in Judah?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:5 says Rehoboam built cities for defence in Judah.

questions.question: Which city is NOT listed as one Rehoboam built according to 2 Chronicles 11?
questions.explanation: Jericho is not mentioned in the list of cities built by Rehoboam in 2 Chronicles 11:6-8.

questions.question: Which of these cities did Rehoboam build first according to the sequence in the chapter?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:6 lists Bethlehem first in the cities Rehoboam built.

questions.question: Which tribe's men did Rehoboam gather warriors from?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:1 states Rehoboam gathered men from the house of Judah and Benjamin.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam obeyed the words of the LORD and returned from going against Jeroboam.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:4 says they obeyed the LORD's words and returned from going against Jeroboam.

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD came to Shemaiah, instructing not to fight against brethren.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:2-4 records the LORD's word to Shemaiah commanding not to fight brethren.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam built cities for agriculture in Judah.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:5 specifies Rehoboam built cities for defence, not agriculture.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam was mentioned as a city that Rehoboam built for defense.
questions.explanation: Jeroboam is a person, not a city, and is not mentioned among the cities Rehoboam built (2 Chronicles 11:6-8).

medium.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Which of the following cities was NOT mentioned as fortified by Rehoboam in 2 Chronicles 11?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:9 mentions Adoraim, Lachish, and Azekah as fortified cities, but Jericho is not listed among them.

questions.question: What does 2 Chronicles 11:10 promise will happen if someone lives in the fenced cities of Judah and Benjamin mentioned in 2 Chronicles 11:9?
options: They will be protected by strongholds
They will be part of the fortified cities
They will be victorious in battle
They will receive blessings from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They will be part of the fortified cities
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:10 lists cities in Judah and Benjamin as fenced cities, implying these cities are fortified as mentioned in 2 Chronicles 11:9.

questions.question: What provisions did Rehoboam put in the strongholds according to 2 Chronicles 11?
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:11 states that he fortified the strongholds and put captains in them along with a store of victual, oil, and wine.

questions.question: How did Rehoboam strengthen the cities according to 2 Chronicles 11:11-12?
options: By building walls and planting vineyards
By appointing captains and providing shields and spears
By making alliances with other nations
questions.correctAnswer: By appointing captains and providing shields and spears
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:11-12 explains that Rehoboam put captains in the strongholds and placed shields and spears in every city, making them very strong.

questions.question: Why did priests and Levites from all Israel come to Rehoboam according to 2 Chronicles 11?
options: Because Jeroboam cast them off from the priest's office
Because they wanted to fight against Jeroboam
Because they wanted to rebel against the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because Jeroboam cast them off from the priest's office
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:13-14 states that priests and Levites came to Rehoboam because Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office unto the LORD.

questions.question: What was Jeroboam's action that caused the Levites to leave their possessions and come to Judah?
options: He ordained priests for high places and calves
He cast them off from executing the priest's office
questions.correctAnswer: He cast them off from executing the priest's office
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:14 explains that the Levites left their possessions and came to Judah because Jeroboam and his sons had cast them off from executing the priest's office.

questions.question: According to 2 Chronicles 11, what did Jeroboam establish that was contrary to proper worship?
options: Priests for high places and calves
A covenant with Judah and Benjamin
A strong army to fight Rehoboam
questions.correctAnswer: Priests for high places and calves
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:15 states that Jeroboam ordained priests for the high places and for the calves which he had made, which was contrary to the LORD's instructions.

questions.question: Who came to Jerusalem to seek the LORD according to 2 Chronicles 11?
options: Those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD
The warriors from Judah and Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: Those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:16 states that those from all the tribes of Israel who set their hearts to seek the LORD came to Jerusalem to sacrifice unto the LORD God of their fathers.

questions.question: What practical lesson can be learned from Rehoboam's actions in fortifying cities and appointing captains?
options: Preparation and leadership are essential for protection
Building walls guarantees peace without effort
Military strength alone ensures God's favor
Ignoring spiritual matters leads to success
questions.correctAnswer: Preparation and leadership are essential for protection
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:11-12 shows that Rehoboam fortified cities and appointed captains, demonstrating the importance of preparation and leadership for protection.

questions.question: How does the departure of the Levites from their possessions to Judah teach about faithfulness in worship?
options: True worship requires sacrifice and commitment
Possessions are more important than serving God
One should avoid change to maintain comfort
Faithfulness is optional in difficult times
questions.correctAnswer: True worship requires sacrifice and commitment
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:14 shows the Levites left their possessions to serve God properly in Judah, teaching that true worship requires sacrifice and commitment.

questions.question: What does Jeroboam's ordaining of priests for calves and high places warn against in Christian living?
options: Creating false worship leads to separation from God
Only sacrifices matter, not the heart
questions.correctAnswer: Creating false worship leads to separation from God
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:15 indicates Jeroboam's false worship practices, warning that such actions cause separation from God.

questions.question: What is the significance of people from all tribes seeking the LORD in Jerusalem despite the division of Israel?
options: God honors those who sincerely seek Him regardless of political divisions
Only the tribe of Judah is acceptable to God
Seeking God is limited to one location only
questions.correctAnswer: God honors those who sincerely seek Him regardless of political divisions
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:16 shows that people from all tribes came to seek the LORD, demonstrating God honors sincere worship regardless of divisions.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam obeyed the LORD's command not to fight against his brethren Israel as recorded in 2 Chronicles 11.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:4 records that Rehoboam obeyed the LORD's word and returned from going to fight against Israel.

questions.question: True or False: According to 2 Chronicles 11, Jeroboam allowed the Levites to continue performing the priest's office unto the LORD in Israel.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:14 states Jeroboam and his sons cast off the Levites from executing the priest's office unto the LORD.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam only fortified the cities of Benjamin and ignored Judah according to 2 Chronicles 11.
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:12 shows that Rehoboam made the cities exceedingly strong having Judah and Benjamin on his side, indicating he fortified both.

hard.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Chronicles Chapter 11.

questions.question: How many years did Rehoboam and his people walk in the way of David and Solomon?
questions.explanation: The text states that they strengthened the kingdom of Judah and made Rehoboam strong for three years, walking in the way of David and Solomon (2 Chronicles 11:17).

questions.question: Who was Rehoboam's wife, the daughter of Jerimoth?
questions.explanation: Rehoboam took Mahalath, the daughter of Jerimoth, to wife (2 Chronicles 11:18).

questions.question: Which of Rehoboam's wives bore him the most children?
questions.explanation: Maachah, the daughter of Absalom, bore Rehoboam several children including Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith (2 Chronicles 11:20).

questions.question: How many wives and concubines did Rehoboam have?
questions.explanation: The text specifies that Rehoboam had eighteen wives and threescore concubines (2 Chronicles 11:21).

questions.question: Who did Rehoboam make chief among his children?
questions.explanation: Rehoboam made Abijah, the son of Maachah, chief among his brethren (2 Chronicles 11:22).

questions.question: What did Rehoboam do with his children throughout Judah and Benjamin?
questions.explanation: Rehoboam wisely dispersed his children throughout all the countries of Judah and Benjamin (2 Chronicles 11:23).

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Mahalath' in 2 Chronicles 11:18 mean?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Mahalath' is often associated with the meaning 'healing' or 'a song of healing'.

questions.question: Which literary device is used when Rehoboam is described as strengthening the kingdom of Judah?
questions.explanation: The strengthening of the kingdom of Judah is presented in a parallel structure to the actions of David and Solomon, illustrating the continuity of leadership.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage connects to the theme of Rehoboam's kingship and God's guidance?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:24 echoes the theme of divine guidance, as it recounts how God instructed Rehoboam not to fight against his brethren, reflecting the same divine sovereignty noted in 2 Chronicles 11:4.

questions.question: Which other passage illustrates the importance of leadership in the context of the people of Israel?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 3:15 speaks of God giving shepherds after His own heart, emphasizing the role of wise leadership as seen in Rehoboam's early reign in 2 Chronicles 11.

questions.question: What comes immediately before the verse where Rehoboam is said to have taken Mahalath as wife?
questions.explanation: The verse immediately preceding 2 Chronicles 11:18 discusses how they strengthened the kingdom of Judah (2 Chronicles 11:17).

questions.question: What comes immediately after the verse where it mentions Rehoboam loved Maachah above all his wives?
questions.explanation: Immediately after stating Rehoboam's love for Maachah, the text explains that he made Abijah the chief among his brethren (2 Chronicles 11:22).

questions.question: Rehoboam's actions in strengthening Judah are reflective of the leadership style of which biblical figure?
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's strengthening of Judah parallels the leadership exemplified by David, as noted in 2 Chronicles 11:17 where they walked in the way of David and Solomon.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam had a total of 88 children.
questions.explanation: Rehoboam had a total of 28 sons and 60 daughters, which sums to 88 children, but the statement is misleading as it does not reflect the accurate count of sons only or daughters alone (2 Chronicles 11:21).

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam was advised by a man of God not to fight against Israel.
questions.explanation: A man of God named Shemaiah advised Rehoboam not to fight against Israel, which he obeyed according to the command of the Lord (2 Chronicles 11:4).

theological.title: 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Chronicles Chapter 11 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does 2 Chronicles 11:4 teach about God's sovereignty in relation to human conflict?
options: God ordains the outcome of political and military conflicts
Human effort alone determines the success of a kingdom
God is indifferent to disputes among His people
Divine intervention is contingent on human prayer
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains the outcome of political and military conflicts
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:4 states, 'for this thing is done of me,' showing that God sovereignly controls the political situation and commands peace among brethren.

questions.question: What doctrine about the priesthood and worship does 2 Chronicles 11:14 teach?
options: True priesthood is dependent on faithfulness to God’s covenant
Priesthood is a hereditary office with no spiritual requirements
Worship practices are valid regardless of who performs them
God accepts worship from all places equally
questions.correctAnswer: True priesthood is dependent on faithfulness to God’s covenant
questions.explanation: Verse 14 explains that the Levites left their possessions because Jeroboam cast them off from priestly duties, showing that legitimate priesthood depends on fidelity to God’s covenant and commands.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sanctification can be drawn from 2 Chronicles 11:17?
options: Walking in the way of David and Solomon reflects a period of covenantal faithfulness
Sanctification is achieved by political strength
Sanctification is irrelevant to leadership success
Human effort alone can sustain holiness
questions.correctAnswer: Walking in the way of David and Solomon reflects a period of covenantal faithfulness
questions.explanation: 2 Chronicles 11:17 states that for three years they walked in the way of David and Solomon, indicating a period of covenantal faithfulness and sanctification in Judah.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does 2 Chronicles 11:4 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The verse 'for this thing is done of me' indicates God’s sovereign control over the political events described.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is exemplified by God’s protection of Judah through fortified cities in 2 Chronicles 11:5?
questions.explanation: God’s providence is demonstrated in His care for Judah’s defense by enabling Rehoboam to build fortified cities.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 11 prepare for the theme of God's faithfulness to Davidic kingship later emphasized in the New Testament?
options: By showing God’s preservation and strengthening of David’s lineage despite political division
By demonstrating the failure of all Davidic kings
By emphasizing the end of Davidic covenant
By highlighting human kingship over divine rule
questions.correctAnswer: By showing God’s preservation and strengthening of David’s lineage despite political division
questions.explanation: The chapter emphasizes Rehoboam’s strength and the support of Levites, showing God’s faithfulness to David’s line, which is foundational for Messianic expectations fulfilled in the New Testament.

questions.question: In what way does 2 Chronicles 11:13–16 connect to the broader biblical narrative of true worship versus idolatry?
options: It contrasts the faithful Levites who follow God with Jeroboam’s idolatrous priesthood
It endorses worship at multiple high places
It shows that worship outside Jerusalem is acceptable
It promotes syncretism in worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts the faithful Levites who follow God with Jeroboam’s idolatrous priesthood
questions.explanation: These verses highlight the Levites leaving Jeroboam’s apostasy to join Rehoboam, emphasizing true worship centered in Jerusalem versus idolatrous practices.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do 2 Chronicles 11:14 and 11:15 teach about the relationship between true priesthood and idolatry?
options: Legitimate priesthood excludes idolatry and must be faithful to God’s commands
Idolatry is a valid alternative form of priesthood
Priesthood is independent of the objects of worship
questions.correctAnswer: Legitimate priesthood excludes idolatry and must be faithful to God’s commands
questions.explanation: Verse 14 shows Levites rejected by Jeroboam due to his idolatrous innovations, and verse 15 describes how Jeroboam ordained priests for idols, contrasting true and false priesthood.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do 2 Chronicles 11:1 and 11:4 provide regarding human initiative and divine command?
options: Human efforts must be subject to divine commands for legitimate outcomes
Human strength alone secures political power
Divine commands are optional in warfare
Human rebellion is justified against divine will
questions.correctAnswer: Human efforts must be subject to divine commands for legitimate outcomes
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows Rehoboam’s military preparation, but verse 4 reveals God’s command to desist, demonstrating that human plans are subordinate to God’s sovereign will.

questions.question: What doctrine about covenantal blessing and leadership is taught by the synthesis of 2 Chronicles 11:17 and 11:22?
options: Covenantal faithfulness leads to the strengthening and orderly succession of leadership
Leadership succession is solely based on human favoritism
Blessing is unrelated to covenantal obedience
questions.correctAnswer: Covenantal faithfulness leads to the strengthening and orderly succession of leadership
questions.explanation: Verse 17 shows strength from covenantal faithfulness, and verse 22 describes Rehoboam preparing Abijah to succeed him, indicating God’s blessing on covenantal leadership.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that 2 Chronicles 11:1–4 condones violence within God's people. What does the passage actually teach?
options: God commands peace among brethren and forbids fighting, overriding human plans for war
God encourages civil war to punish disobedience
The passage is neutral on violence among brethren
God permits violence if politically necessary
questions.correctAnswer: God commands peace among brethren and forbids fighting, overriding human plans for war
questions.explanation: Verses 1–4 show Rehoboam preparing for war but God commands through Shemaiah not to fight brethren, demonstrating God’s preference for peace among His people.

questions.question: What doctrine about divine provision and leadership training is taught in 2 Chronicles 11:23?
options: God blesses leaders who wisely distribute resources and prepare their heirs for governance
Leaders must hoard resources for personal gain
Provision is irrelevant to leadership success
Divine blessing is unrelated to family and political strategy
questions.correctAnswer: God blesses leaders who wisely distribute resources and prepare their heirs for governance
questions.explanation: Verse 23 describes Rehoboam wisely dispersing his children with victuals, reflecting God’s blessing on prudent leadership preparation.

questions.question: What combined attribute of God is demonstrated in 2 Chronicles 11:13 and 11:16 through the movement of priests and worshippers to Jerusalem?
options: God’s covenant faithfulness and holiness in preserving true worship
God’s wrath and judgment on all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant faithfulness and holiness in preserving true worship
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 16 show the faithful priests and people seeking the LORD in Jerusalem, highlighting God’s commitment to covenant worship and holiness.

questions.question: How does 2 Chronicles 11:21 illustrate the theological tension between divine blessing and human sinfulness?
options: It shows God’s blessing of children despite Rehoboam’s polygamy and potential moral compromise
It endorses polygamy as a divine ideal
It condemns Rehoboam’s family life entirely
It disconnects blessing from moral conduct
questions.correctAnswer: It shows God’s blessing of children despite Rehoboam’s polygamy and potential moral compromise
questions.explanation: Verse 21 notes Rehoboam’s many wives and children, reflecting both divine blessing in offspring and the ongoing tension with human sinfulness in leadership.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding the role of prophecy and divine communication is evident in 2 Chronicles 11:2–3?
options: God communicates His will through prophets to guide kings and the people
Prophets are unnecessary for political decisions
Kings receive divine messages through dreams only
Divine communication is private and not disclosed publicly
questions.correctAnswer: God communicates His will through prophets to guide kings and the people
questions.explanation: Verses 2–3 show the LORD speaking to Shemaiah, who then conveys God’s message to Rehoboam and the people, affirming the prophetic role.
